Subject: Private offer anchor variance and reseller split (NimbleGrid)

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to outline the ask in a single thread so we can share with finance and our reseller. Two quick items:  

1) Anchor / list price variance: we have two internal use cases (ad inference + reranking) that will run across AWS and GCP. Your sales contact proposed a single list price anchor for the private offer, but we expect materially different effective costs across clouds. Can Redwood provide guidance or a cadence for separate anchors per cloud (or a blended anchor approach)?

2) Reseller split: our reseller (StellarCloud Partners) needs visibility into the net-back they will receive after passback. We need a simple waterfall showing list price, Redwood discount, reseller commission, and any marketplace fees.

I've attached expected-monthly-usage (nimblegrid-expected-usage.csv) and a short term-sheet sketch (RDW-private-offer-draft-v1.pdf). Can we get an initial response by EOD Wednesday?

Appreciate it,
Samir

Subject: Re: Private offer anchor variance and reseller split (NimbleGrid)

Samir —

Thanks for the clear ask and the files. Quick answers up front, then proposed next steps: 

Short answer on anchors: we can do either per-cloud anchors or a blended anchor; each has trade-offs. Per-cloud anchors more closely reflect list pricing and reseller passback mechanics but add operational complexity for you and StellarCloud. Blended anchors simplify negotiation but can create perceived unfairness if usage skews to one cloud.

Reseller waterfall: we can provide a waterfall template that shows list price -> Redwood private offer discount -> marketplace fee (if applicable) -> reseller commission -> customer net. We’ll need a few inputs: whether StellarCloud expects commission as percentage of list or percentage of Redwood's revenue, and whether marketplace passback is applied pre- or post-discount.

Proposed next steps:
- Ben (cc) to draft a two-page waterfall template and a per-cloud vs blended anchor pros/cons table.
- Marissa (cc) to validate any marketplace fee assumptions for AWS and GCP (we often see different listing fees).
- Connor to follow up with NimbleGrid by EOD Wed with an initial proposal.

If that timeline works, we’ll send a short deck and waterfall for your finance + StellarCloud.

Best,
Connor O’Brien
Director, Cloud Sales — Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

Connor / Marissa —

Attached is a quick waterfall template (I'll publish to Drive after we iterate) and my recommendation: start with per-cloud anchors for this deal. Reasoning:

- NimbleGrid's usage profile shows a ~2.7x cost difference (GCP higher on our current quoting) between clouds for equivalent throughput. A single blended anchor will need a large buffer and could compress reseller economics unpredictably.
- StellarCloud typically expects commission as a % of list price (they resell under marketplace terms). If we set list price per cloud, passback math is straightforward and auditable.
- Ops: we can implement per-cloud anchors without major platform changes; the private offer model supports region-specific SKU anchoring.

Questions for NimbleGrid:
1) Confirm whether StellarCloud wants commission % on list price or net after Redwood discount.
2) Any compliance constraint that requires a single customer-facing bill (we can still show the waterfall internally).

I'll draft the two-slide pros/cons + waterfall by EOD.

Ben

- The waterfall CSV will include columns: month, cloud, list_price, private_offer_discount, marketplace_fee, reseller_commission_pct, reseller_commission_amount, customer_net. We will pull data from our billing export and the private offer mapping.
